arxiv-1905-06334.title: String percolation in AA and pp collisions
arxiv-1905-06334.creator: I. Bautista, C. Pajares, J. E. Ramírez
arxiv-1905-06334.description: Abstract A brief review of the string percolation model and its results are presented together with the comparison to experimental data. First, it is done an introduction to the quark-gluon phase diagram and the lattice results concerning the confinement and the percolation of center domains.

arxiv-2208-04740.title: Aesthetic Language Guidance Generation of Images Using Attribute Comparison DOI: 10.1145/1122445.1122456 Journal: JACM Volume: 37 4 111 8 Thanks: *Corresponding authors CCS: Applied computing Media arts
arxiv-2208-04740.creator: Xin Jin, Qiang Deng, Jianwen Lv, Heng Huang, Hao Lou, Chaoen Xiao ∗
arxiv-2208-04740.description: Abstract . With the vigorous development of mobile photography technology, major mobile phone manufacturers are scrambling to improve the shooting ability of equipments and the photo beautification algorithm of software. However, the improvement of intelligent equipments and algorithms cannot replace human subjective photography technology. In this paper, we propose the aesthetic language guidance of image (ALG).

arxiv-2301-09729.title: Long-term stable Electromyography classification using Canonical Correlation Analysis
arxiv-2301-09729.creator: Elisa Donati, Simone Benatti, Enea Ceolini, Giacomo Indiveri
arxiv-2301-09729.description: Abstract Discrimination of hand gestures based on the decoding of surface electromyography (sEMG) signals is a well-establish approach for controlling prosthetic devices and for Human-Machine Interfaces (HMI). However, despite the promising results achieved by this approach in well-controlled experimental conditions, its deployment in long-term real-world application scenarios is still hindered by several challenges.

arxiv-2304-04280.title: FrenchMedMCQA: A French Multiple-Choice Question Answering Dataset for Medical domain
arxiv-2304-04280.creator: Yanis Labrak, Adrien Bazoge, Richard Dufour, Béatrice Daille, Pierre-Antoine Gourraud, Emmanuel Morin, Mickael Rouvier, LIA - Avignon University first.lastname@univ-avignon.fr, LS2N - Nantes University first.lastname@univ-nantes.fr, CHU de Nantes - La clinique des données - Nantes University, Zenido
arxiv-2304-04280.description: Abstract This paper introduces FrenchMedMCQA, the first publicly available Multiple-Choice Question Answering (MCQA) dataset in French for medical domain. It is composed of 3,105 questions taken from real exams of the French medical specialization diploma in pharmacy, mixing single and multiple answers. Each instance of the dataset contains an identifier, a question, five possible answers and their manual correction(s).

arxiv-2403-02831.title: SpaceHopper: A Small-Scale Legged Robot for Exploring Low-Gravity Celestial Bodies
arxiv-2403-02831.creator: Alexander Spiridonov, Fabio Buehler, Moriz Berclaz, Valerio Schelbert, Jorit Geurts, Elena Krasnova
arxiv-2403-02831.description: Abstract We present SpaceHopper , a three-legged, small-scale robot designed for future mobile exploration of asteroids and moons. The robot weighs 5.2 kg 5.2\text{\,}\mathrm{kg} and has a body size of 245 mm 245\text{\,}\mathrm{mm} while using space-qualifiable components. Furthermore, SpaceHopper ’s design and controls make it well-adapted for investigating dynamic locomotion modes with extended flight-phases.

arxiv-2404-12811.title: Black Hole shadows of α ′ \alpha^{\prime} -corrected black holes
arxiv-2404-12811.creator: F. Agurto-Sepúlveda 1,2, J. Oliva 1, M. Oyarzo 1,3, D.R.G Schleicher 2
arxiv-2404-12811.description: Abstract In this paper we study the qualitative features induces by corrections to GR coming from String Theory, on the shadows of rotating black holes. We deal with the slowly rotating black hole solutions up to order 𝒪 ⁡ ( a 3 ) \mathcal{O}(a^{3}) , to first order in α ′ \alpha^{\prime} , including also the dilaton.

arxiv-2408-17359.title: Including photoexcitation explicitly in trajectory-based nonadiabatic dynamics at no cost
arxiv-2408-17359.creator: Jiří Janoš, Petr Slavíček, Basile F. E. Curchod
arxiv-2408-17359.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jiří Janoš, Petr Slavíček, Basile F. E. Curchod. Over the last decades, theoretical photochemistry has produced multiple techniques to simulate the nonadiabatic dynamics of molecules. Surprisingly, much less effort has been devoted to adequately describing the first step of a photochemical or photophysical process: photoexcitation. Here, we propose a formalism to include the effect of a laser pulse in trajectory-based nonadiabatic dynamics at the level of the initial conditions, with no additional cost.

arxiv-2502-12892.title: Archetypal SAE: Adaptive and Stable Dictionary Learning for Concept Extraction in Large Vision Models
arxiv-2502-12892.description: Abstract Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) have emerged as a powerful framework for machine learning interpretability, enabling the unsupervised decomposition of model representations into a dictionary of abstract, human-interpretable concepts. However, we reveal a fundamental limitation: existing SAEs exhibit severe instability, as identical models trained on similar datasets can produce sharply different dictionaries, undermining their reliability as an interpretability tool.

arxiv-2503-15478.title: SWEET-RL: Training Multi-Turn LLM Agents on Collaborative Reasoning Tasks
arxiv-2503-15478.creator: Yifei Zhou, Song Jiang, Yuandong Tian, Jason Weston, Sergey Levine, Sainbayar Sukhbaatar, Xian Li
arxiv-2503-15478.description: Abstract Large language model (LLM) agents need to perform multi-turn interactions in real-world tasks. However, existing multi-turn RL algorithms for optimizing LLM agents fail to perform effective credit assignment over multiple turns while leveraging the generalization capabilities of LLMs and it remains unclear how to develop such algorithms.

arxiv-2504-15510.title: Ridge-Regularized Largest Root Test For High-Dimensional General Linear Hypotheses
arxiv-2504-15510.creator: Haoran Li
arxiv-2504-15510.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Haoran Li. A fundamental problem in multivariate analysis is testing general linear hypotheses for regression coefficients in a multivariate linear model. This framework includes many important tasks such as MANOVA, joint significance testing, and detecting trends or seasonal effects. Roy’s largest root test is a classical and powerful method for detecting concentrated signals, based on the largest eigenvalue of an F F -matrix constructed from residual covariance matrices. However, in high-dimensional settings, these matrices often become ill-conditioned or singular, making the test infeasible.

arxiv-2506-07898.title: Constraints on Quaoar’s rings and atmosphere from JWST/NIRCam observations of a stellar occultation
arxiv-2506-07898.creator: Benjamin C.N. Proudfoot, Bryan J. Holler, Ko Arimatsu, Flavia L. Rommel, Cameron Collyer, Estela Fernández-Valenzuela
arxiv-2506-07898.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Benjamin C.N. Proudfoot, Bryan J. Holler, Ko Arimatsu, Flavia L. Rommel, Cameron Collyer, Estela Fernández-Valenzuela. Observations of stellar occultations have revealed that small bodies are capable of hosting ring systems. The trans-Neptunian object (TNO) Quaoar, is the host of an enigmatic ring system, with two rings located well-outside the Roche limit. To better understand these structures, we observed a stellar occultation by Quaoar and its rings using the James Webb Space Telescope’s (JWST) NIRCam instrument.

arxiv-2508-17343.title: Agentic AI for Software: thoughts from Software Engineering community
arxiv-2508-17343.creator: Abhik Roychoudhury
arxiv-2508-17343.description: Abstract AI agents have recently shown significant promise in software engineering. Much public attention has been transfixed on the topic of code generation from Large Language Models (LLMs) via a prompt. However, software engineering is much more than programming, and AI agents go far beyond instructions given by a prompt.

arxiv-2510-13814.title: Reversing The Lens: Using Explainable AI To Understand Human Expertise
arxiv-2510-13814.creator: Roussel Rahman, Aashwin Ananda Mishra, Wan-Lin Hu
arxiv-2510-13814.description: Abstract Both humans and machine learning models learn from experience, particularly in safety- and reliability-critical domains. While psychology seeks to understand human cognition, the field of Explainable AI (XAI) develops methods to interpret machine learning models. This study bridges these domains by applying computational tools from XAI to analyze human learning.

arxiv-2511-06220.title: HYDRA: A Hybrid Heuristic-Guided Deep Representation Architecture for Predicting Latent Zero-Day Vulnerabilities in Patched Functions
arxiv-2511-06220.creator: Mohammad Farhad, Sabbir Rahman, Shuvalaxmi Dass
arxiv-2511-06220.description: Abstract . Software security testing, particularly when enhanced with deep learning models, has become a powerful approach for improving software quality, enabling faster detection of known flaws in source code. However, many approaches miss post-fix latent vulnerabilities that remain even after patches typically due to incomplete fixes or overlooked issues may later lead to zero-day exploits.

europmc-pmc8185188.title: Recurrent emergence of SARS-CoV-2 spike deletion H69/V70 and its role in the Alpha variant B.1.1.7.
europmc-pmc8185188.creator: Meng B, Kemp SA, Papa G, Datir R, Ferreira IATM, Marelli S, Harvey WT, Lytras S, Mohamed A, Gallo G, Thakur N, Collier DA, Mlcochova P, COVID-19 Genomics UK (COG-UK) Consortium, Duncan LM, Carabelli AM, Kenyon JC, Lever AM, De Marco A, Saliba C, Culap K, Cameroni E, Matheson NJ, Piccoli L, Corti D, James LC, Robertson DL, Bailey D, Gupta RK.
europmc-pmc8185188.description: We report severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike ΔH69/V70 in multiple independent lineages, often occurring after acquisition of receptor binding motif replacements such as N439K and Y453F, known to increase binding affinity to the ACE2 receptor and...

gao-gaoreports-gao-05-327.title: Protection of Chemical and Water Infrastructure: Federal Requirements, Actions of Selected Facilities, and Remaining Challenges
gao-gaoreports-gao-05-327.creator: U.S. Government Accountability Office
gao-gaoreports-gao-05-327.description: Protection of Chemical and Water Infrastructure: Federal Requirements, Actions of Selected Facilities, and Remaining Cha (n.d.). Declassified document.

pmc-11362096.title: Pulmonary embolism incidence among patient admitted under psychiatry department: a case-control study
pmc-11362096.creator: Wanling Zhang, Dhirendra Paudel, Rui Shi, Junwei Yang, Jingwen Liu, Yanbin Jia
pmc-11362096.description: BackgroundPulmonary embolism (PE) is a serious and potentially life-threatening condition that requires prompt diagnosis and treatment. Identifying risk factors and diagnostic markers can aid in the early detection and management of this condition.MethodsThis case-control study examined 10,077 patients admitted to Shenzhen Kangning Hospital’s psychiatry facility in 2020. Among these, 65 patients were diagnosed with PE, including 50 new cases.

pmc-11514680.title: Establishing prognostic models for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma based on immune cells
pmc-11514680.creator: Zhuo-Ran Wang, Cun-Zhen Zhang, Zhan Ding, Yi-Zhuo Li, Jian-Hua Yin, Nan Li
pmc-11514680.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) is a malignant liver tumor that is challenging to treat and manage and current prognostic models for the disease are inefficient or ineffective. Tumor-associated immune cells are critical for tumor development and progression.

pmc-11561213.title: Burden of Current Insulin Therapy and Expectations for Future Insulin Therapy: Results from INBEING, a Web-Based Survey in Japan
pmc-11561213.creator: Yasuaki Hayashino, Satoshi Tsuboi, Yuiko Yamamoto, Hitoshi Ishii
pmc-11561213.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionThis survey assessed the perspectives of physicians, people with diabetes (PWD), and caregivers in Japan regarding initiation barriers and treatment burden associated with insulin therapy, and expectations for new insulin therapies.MethodsAn online survey, conducted May–June 2023, was completed by physicians (n = 411), PWD (type 1 diabetes, n = 108; type 2 diabetes [T2D]: insulin-naive, n = 114; insulin-treated, n = 108), and caregivers (family members, n = 107; nurses, n = 117; care workers, n = 104).

pmc-11635248.title: Postoperative day of surgery ambulation improves outcomes following lung resection: a multicenter prospective cohort study
pmc-11635248.creator: Christina M. Stuart, Adam R. Dyas, Nicole M. Mott, Kyle E. Bata, Michael R. Bronsert, Alyson D. Kelleher, Katherine O. McCabe, Crystal Erickson, Simran K. Randhawa, Elizabeth A. David, John D. Mitchell, Robert A. Meguid
pmc-11635248.description: BackgroundThe impact of post-surgical same day ambulation in lung resection patients is relatively unstudied. We sought to determine the relationship between day of surgery ambulation and postoperative outcomes after lung resection.MethodsThis was a prospective cohort study at one healthcare system with six hospitals (1/2019–3/2023). Patients undergoing segmentectomy and lobectomy were targeted for inclusion.

pmc-12615241.title: A photovoltaic panel cleaning robot with a lightweight YOLO v8
pmc-12615241.creator: Jidong Luo, Guoyi Wang, Yanjiao Lei, Dong Wang, Yayong Chen, Hongzhou Zhang
pmc-12615241.description: Cleaning PV (photovoltaic) panels is essential for a PV station, as dirt or dust reduces the effective irradiation of solar energy and weakens the efficiency of converting solar energy into free electrons. The inconsistent (cleaning efficacy) and unsafe (summarized voltage and current) manual method is a challenge for a PV station.

pmc-12929162.title: Clopidogrel-induced drug-induced hypersensitivity syndrome following percutaneous coronary intervention: a case report of therapeutic dilemma and management strategy
pmc-12929162.creator: Sikun Wang, Jiang Zhou, Yuanhua Sun
pmc-12929162.description: BackgroundDrug-induced hypersensitivity syndrome (DIHS), also known as drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS), is a rare but potentially life-threatening adverse drug reaction. Clopidogrel induced DHS following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) presents a unique therapeutic challenge due to the critical need for dual antiplatelet therapy to prevent stent thrombosis.

pmc-12979075.title: Ziyuglycoside II ameliorates chemotherapy-induced neutropenia by promoting neutrophil differentiation and functional recovery via SPI1 and C/EBPϵ transcriptional regulation
pmc-12979075.creator: Lingdi Li, Huan Lei, Luqi Chen, Chunye Cao, Haolin He, Yanfeng Zhang, Lin Zhang, Liang Peng, Yuxiu Yang, Yulin Feng, Haihong Fang
pmc-12979075.description: BackgroundChemotherapy-induced neutropenia (CIN) remains a major dose-limiting toxicity associated with myelosuppressive chemotherapy regimens. The development of therapeutic strategies capable of effectively restoring neutrophil production and function could address a critical unmet clinical issue. ZGSII, a bioactive compound derived from Sanguisorba officinalis, has shown potential in ameliorating leukopenia.

pmc-13068505.title: The Humanistic Care Behaviour of Head Nurses and the Influence on Stress and Transition Shock of New Nurses: A Cross‐Sectional Study
pmc-13068505.creator: Yuhong Luo, Bei Yun, Wenjing Ling, Wen Fang, Shoubi Wang, Chaoting Zhen, Yaling Li
pmc-13068505.description: AimTo examine the interrelationships among head nurses' humanistic care behaviour, job rotation stress, and transition shock among new nurses in Southwest China.DesignThis study employed a cross‐sectional observational research design.MethodsA total of 1128 new nurses were recruited from ten tertiary hospitals in Guizhou Province between March and September 2022.

pmc-13185239.title: Neurocognitive function profiles in Chinese patients with melancholic vs. non-melancholic major depressive disorder
pmc-13185239.creator: Li-Min Xin, Jing-Yu Lin, Hong-Zhen Fan, FengYan, Xin Yu, Yun-Ai Su, Tian-Mei Si
pmc-13185239.description: BackgroundThe study aimed to investigate the neurocognitive characteristics of Chinese patients with melancholic depression (MEL) versus non-melancholic depression (NMEL).MethodsData were derived from a multicenter, multiphase prospective study conducted across nine top-tier hospitals in six provinces of China. A total of 287 healthy controls (HCs), 643 patients with major depressive disorder (MDD) were included.

pmc-13217211.title: Food protein-induced enterocolitis syndrome in children: An updated review on pathogenesis, diagnosis, and management
pmc-13217211.creator: Khadija Alshehhi, Rahaf Abughosh, Gawahir Abdelrahman, Abdalqader Abujouda, Ahmed Elghoudi, Rana Bitar
pmc-13217211.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Food protein-induced enterocolitis syndrome (FPIES) is a severe non-IgE-mediated food allergy with unclear prevalence and pathophysiology. FPIES typically presents in the first year of life but can present later in adulthood in an acute or chronic manner. Acute FPIES manifests 1-4 hours after ingestion of foods such as rice, oats, and cow’s milk, causing repetitive vomiting, diarrhea, lethargy, dehydration, and hypovolemic shock. Interestingly, affected infants are generally mistakenly diagnosed with sepsis or viral gastroenteritis.

pmc-13277125.title: A social cognitive perspective on teacher technology self-efficacy, inclusion, and student aspirations
pmc-13277125.creator: Huang Lei, Fang Na, Liu Lu, Hassan Jawad Soomro, Ghulam Hussain Khan Zaigham
pmc-13277125.description: This study examines how digital inclusion at the school level shapes the relationship between teacher technology-integration self-efficacy and students’ aspirations for upward mobility. Drawing on social cognitive theory, we propose that confident teachers create inclusive classroom environments that foster student engagement and long-term educational aspirations, and that these effects are strengthened when schools provide systemic support for digital technology.

pmc-13350709.title: Lab perceptual training and robot-assisted training in improving speech prosody of autistic children
pmc-13350709.creator: Si Chen, Bruce Xiao Wang, James Chung-Wai Cheung, Fang Zhou, Yitian Hong, Bei Li, Angel Chan, Tempo Po Yi Tang, Bin Li, Zhuoming Chen, Chunyi Wen
pmc-13350709.description: Children with autism spectrum disorder are known to exhibit both social and language difficulties. Speech prosody is known to be easily noticeable, which has been shown to have far-reaching influences in the academic and social life of autistic individuals. This study examined two training programs on the speech prosody of autistic children, who tend to avoid social speech signals.

pmc-13448028.title: Activation of BMPR1b–SMAD pathway by Ginsenoside F1 restores osteoblast function in ovariectomy-induced osteoporosis
pmc-13448028.creator: Sulagna Mukherjee, Il-Gyu Ko, Soo-Young Park, Min-Hee Seo, Seung-Soon Im
pmc-13448028.description: IntroductionOsteoblasts are bone-building cells that drive osteogenesis by producing osteoid and promoting its mineralization during development and remodeling. Although ginsenosides from Panax species can enhance bone formation and inhibit resorption, the role of ginsenoside F1 in osteoblast differentiation and bone metabolism has not been defined.

pmc-13556895.title: 751. Transcranial Pulse Stimulation (TPS) suitable add-on treatment of patients with psychiatric disorders?
pmc-13556895.creator: C A Penkov, V Rößner-Ruff, J Krieger, K Friedrich, M Ziegenbein
pmc-13556895.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundNeurostimulation procedures have been used for some time to treat neurological and neuropsychiatric disorders. Several methods of non-invasive brain stimulation have been investigated, including transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), transcranial electrical stimulation (tES), and transcranial pulse stimulation (TPS). While TMS and tES have been studied more extensively, particularly in relation to Alzheimer's disease (AD), there is an urgent need for further research into TPS. Some studies have demonstrated favourable outcomes when these methods were employed.

pmc-13675871.title: Nutrition Care and Dietetic Practice in Managing Metabolic and Endocrine Dysfunction in Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS): Implications and Opportunities in the Context of the Name Change of Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome to PMOS☆
pmc-13675871.creator: Donna Vine, Lisa Moran, Helena Teede, Mahnaz Bahri-Khomami
pmc-13675871.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) affects 8‒13% of women across the lifespan. Those with PMOS have reduced quality of life and increased risk of comorbidities, including elevated weight, eating disorders, gestational diabetes, type 2 diabetes, and cardiovascular disease. PMOS is a major population in clinical dietetic practice, and dietary intervention is the first-line approach recommended to target metabolic risk in the international evidence-based guidelines for assessment and management of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).

pmc-13676997.title: Multiscale Regulation of Ru‐Based Catalysts for Upgrading Biomass‐Derived Levulinic Acid and Levulinates to γ‐Valerolactone: Mechanisms, Advances, and Challenges
pmc-13676997.creator: Xin Ni, Cailu Xiao, Gongbing Zhou, Jingzi Zhang
pmc-13676997.description: γ‐Valerolactone (GVL) serves as a bridge connecting biomass‐derived levulinic acid (LA) and its esters to value‐added chemicals. Ru‐based catalysts exhibit high efficiency for LA/levulinates‐to‐GVL conversion, owing to their strong C═O activation ability, excellent GVL selectivity, and compatibility to diverse hydrogen sources such as H2, formic acid (FA), and alcohols.

uslaw-usc-t10-s7440.title: 10 U.S.C. § 7440 — Quartermaster
uslaw-usc-t10-s7440.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s7440.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part III (Training); Chapter 753 (United States Military Academy). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Secretary of the Army shall detail a commissioned officer of the Army as quartermaster for the Corps of Cadets. The quartermaster shall— (1) buy and issue all supplies for the cadets; (2) buy and issue all provisions for the mess.
